table.title: State of the Chinese Army on August 31, 1912—continued
footnotes: 1 Kung Wei Chun.—President Yuan Shih-kai re-enlisted a large portion of the old Wu Wei Yu Chun, principally from Honan, and in May their name was changed to Kung Wei Chun.
2 Wu Wei Tso Chun.—General Chang Kuei-tih's Tungchow troops.

4 Huai Chun.—Troops enlisted from the neighbourhood of the Huai River, in Anhui, who have been in existence for a considerable time, and have been used principally, for police purposes on the railways.
5 Wu Wei Chien Chun —General Chang Hsun's troops, composed partly of the original forces he withdrew from Nanking, and partly of recruits.
7 Sung Hsien Detachment.—From Sung Hsien district.
10 Kuang Fu Chun (Glorious Restoration Army).—Recruited at Shanghai during the revolution. Part dispatched to Nanking and part to Chefoo.
12 Pei Fa Chun (Northern Punitive Force).—Raised in Kueichow during the revolution, as an expeditionary force against the North.
13 Lu Ying.—A remnant of the old Green Flag Army, of no fighting value.
table.context: The table gives the strength of the Chinese army in Sinkiang and the totals for August 31, 1912, by unit type, with footnotes identifying the troop origins.
